title: Nutrition Q&A #3
summary: NH answers viewer nutrition questions: why supermarket produce is low in nutrients, eating less on rest days, what to do about bloat on a bulk, sweeteners, his low-protein, high-carb diet, his minimal supplements, orthorexia and training around religious fasts. He also argues that measuring body fat is pointless and that the best body fat range for growth is genetic.
claims: Supermarket produce is low in micronutrients because year-round farming drains soil minerals that fallow periods used to restore; fertilisers make plants grow without restoring their nutrition
Tomatoes and cucumbers grown in fertile soil taste far better; supermarket ones taste like water because they are nutrient-poor
He admits he has no source for the claim about produce
He likes a full stomach on lower body days because hunger hurts his focus, and tends to eat more carbs on upper body days; these are preferences to experiment with
Eat less on rest days: he eats mostly protein and non-starchy vegetables with carbs near zero, unless you are a hardgainer
Find your own macros instead of following set quotas; he eats lots of carbs, almost no fat and a little protein
If a bulk only produces bloat with no visible muscle gain, your body has tapped out; switch to maintenance or a small deficit
Overly enthusiastic bulks cause yo-yo bulk-and-cut cycles that lead nowhere; every bulk is just the first half of a cut
Artificial sweeteners like stevia are not harmless; the real danger is addiction to sweetness, so ask yourself why you need food to taste sweet
Western culture links childhood with sugar (Halloween candy, Sunny D), which explains adults' addiction to sweet tastes
To work around nutrient-poor produce, find farmers who rest their soil, favour hardy root vegetables like potatoes over thin-skinned ones, or grow your own garden
He eats about 70 g of protein a day at most; eating much more caused him health problems and no extra gains
His protein spread: about 35-40 g at dinner plus two snacks of about 20 g each
He used to eat 12 eggs and 500 g of red meat a day; he has since cut red meat, dairy and pork and now eats mostly chicken, turkey, salmon, sardines, tuna, eggs, lentils and beans
Natural supplement stacks are copied from PED users; when he cut 80% of his stack nothing changed, so cut yours in half
Only three supplements work for him: creatine, MSM powder and bee pollen, the last taken six months a year; the most expensive, most hyped supplements tend to be garbage
He takes raw garlic and ginger and recommends trying tonic herbs instead of supplements
The orthorexia label pathologises healthy eating; a whole-food diet is normal, though obsessing over clean eating can become a disorder
Eating only for pleasure while ignoring the consequences is close to addiction
You can make gains without meat; during religious meat restrictions, eggs and fish are good replacements, and red meat is not necessary
You can still make gains, though not optimal ones, while lifting through Ramadan or religious fasts; spirituality can take priority for a few months
Measuring body fat is useless and there is no best method; just focus on looking good and feeling good
Influencers use body fat drops such as 18% to 13% to sell programs and supplements
The best body fat range for building muscle is genetic; some people grow well at 11-12%, while he is sure he would suffer at 10%
To find your lowest healthy body fat, reach a size you like and then recomp slowly until fat loss stalls; he is still recomping at 210 lb and might bulk again in 4-5 years
